svg.title: From gene structures to an evolutionary model
svg.desc: Each aligned region defines a character. Its states are observed at species and inferred at ancestral nodes. Original synthetic example; not a biological validation.
svg.text: From gene structures to an evolutionary model
Each aligned region defines a character. Its states are observed at species and inferred at ancestral nodes.
SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE | Genomic distances are schematic | IntraPhy 0.18
? = unresolved state; N/A = no corresponding DNA on which to define exonic status.
Model a character along a branch
Infer ancestral states on the species tree
Example: intron presence at the highlighted position
Branch length t and rates determine transition probabilities.
Within a gene family, each character class shares rates.
Whole transcripts are not the states of this model.
Sum over alternative ancestral states; do not choose a single history
before calculating the likelihood. Unknown tips allow both states.
Filled fraction: probability of ancestral intron presence.
Illustrative fixed rates, not estimates: g = 0.4, l = 0.2;
internal branches = 0.4, terminal branches = 1; root P(1) = 2/3. Tree not to scale.
